test_title: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper (Held On: 12th September 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the legal nature of the Right to Property under Article 300A?

options.text: The State can take property without any legal basis
A constitutional legal right allowing deprivation only by law
Enforceable by Article 32 before the Supreme Court

solution:
The correct answer is __**A constitutional legal right allowing deprivation only by law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Article 300A of the Constitution:** This article was inserted by the **44th Amendment Act of 1978**. It ensures that **no person shall be deprived of their property except by authority of law**. It replaced the earlier provision of the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right. *Hence, the right is now a constitutional legal right.*
 
• The Right to Property is no longer a **Fundamental Right**. It was removed from Part III of the Constitution and placed under Part XII as a constitutional right. *Hence, it is not enforceable under Article 32.*
 
• The State cannot take property without a legal basis. Article 300A explicitly states that **deprivation of property can only occur through a law enacted by the legislature**. *This ensures protection against arbitrary deprivation.*
